title: Interview Practice, Follow-Up & Professional Presence
summary: Bring the unit together through interview practice, professional communication, reflection, and appropriate follow-up after an interview or career conversation.
objectives: Practice answering common interview questions with truthful examples.
Demonstrate professional listening and communication during a simulated interview.
Create an appropriate follow-up message and identify improvements for future interviews.

vocab.def: A practice interview designed to help someone prepare for a real interview.
Professional communication after a meeting or interview that acknowledges the conversation or confirms next steps.
Reviewing an experience to identify strengths, gaps, lessons, and possible improvements.
The specific action expected after an interview, application, meeting, or career conversation.

sections.heading: Practice should improve clarity, not create a script
sections.body: Practice can help you organize your thoughts and remember useful examples. The goal is not to memorize every word or sound artificial.

sections.heading: Listening changes the quality of your answer
sections.body: Pause long enough to understand the question, ask for clarification when needed, and answer the question actually being asked.

sections.heading: Professional follow-up can be simple
sections.body: A short follow-up message can thank the interviewer, reference the conversation, restate interest accurately, and acknowledge any stated next step.

sections.heading: Every interview can produce useful learning
sections.body: Afterward, review what went well, where answers were unclear, what information you still need, and what you would improve before the next conversation.

practice.prompt: You realize after an interview that one answer was unclear. What can you do?
practice.answer: Reflect on the answer, improve how you would explain it next time, and use appropriate follow-up if clarification is genuinely needed.

practice.prompt: Should a thank-you message claim that you are guaranteed to get the position?
practice.answer: No. It should remain professional and accurate without assuming a hiring decision.

lab.objective: Complete a simulated interview, review feedback, identify two strengths and two areas for improvement, and draft a short professional follow-up message.
